source: These are AI video formats, the set this page can teach. YouTube has on the order of 70 to 80 core niches and thousands of micro-niches. A faceless reel that lists city docs or car hacks is a different list. Dollar lines are 500,000 views times a published RPM band, not a payout.

niches.name: AI baby comedy
niches.about: One baby, an adult voice, a four-line joke. The face stays the same.
niches.lasts: A one-off baby stops getting views in about a week. The same face, voice, and room can keep going.
steps: Make one baby face and save it. Do not start from a real child's photo.
Pick one room and keep it. A new set every episode looks like a new channel.
Write four lines only: a request, a pause, a complaint, a last line that flips the request.
Record those four lines in your own voice. Do not clone a real person's voice.
Turn the still into a talking clip. Caption every line in big type.
Turn on the AI label. The next episode uses the same baby and the same room.
niches.shape:
Baby: you cut it?
Worker: yes.
Baby: why?
Worker: the last line answers a different question than the one the baby asked.
niches.tools: A still generator, your own voice, a talking-photo tool, CapCut.
niches.avoid: A real child's face, a copied voice, or another channel's exact story.

niches.name: Two babies talking
niches.about: Two saved faces argue. The joke is in the third reply, not the setup.
niches.lasts: Compilations of random babies get one spike. A pair with names can be a series.
steps: Save two faces. Give them names and do not change them.
Write three exchanges. The third one is the joke. Cut anything before that.
Record both voices yourself, different pitch, same mic.
Cut on each line. Do not hold a face while the other talks.
Caption the names once, then the lines.
Label it AI. Next episode is the same pair in the same place.
niches.shape:
A asks for one thing.
B gives the wrong thing, twice.
A gets angry.
B's last line shows A was saying the helper's name, not the thing.
niches.tools: Two stills, your voice twice, CapCut.
niches.avoid: A new pair every upload, or a real child's photo as either face.

niches.name: Horror episodes
niches.about: Numbered episodes. A normal start, one wrong detail, a last line.
niches.lasts: One jump-scare dies faster than a numbered series.
steps: Put the episode number on screen from the first second.
Write a normal first line. Someone is home, or having tea, or on a call.
Add one detail that is wrong. Do not explain it in the middle.
Use three stills. Cut when the sentence changes, not on a timer.
Keep one narrator voice for the whole series.
End on the line that reframes the start. Stop. Label it AI.
niches.shape: Episode 4. She is drinking tea. The clock says 1:30. The last line is about who poured it.
niches.tools: A still generator, one voice, CapCut.
niches.avoid: Gore close-ups, a new narrator every episode, and explaining the twist after it lands.

niches.name: AI mythology
niches.about: One scene from a known story. Same art style every episode.
niches.lasts: One myth clip can spike. The art style lasts longer than a new god every upload.
steps: Pick one event. Not the whole epic.
Open on the conflict in the first two seconds. Skip the family tree.
Lock one art style and reuse it. A new look every week is a new channel.
Write the voiceover first, then make stills that match the lines.
Caption every line. Keep music under the voice.
Label it AI. The next episode is the next event, same style.
niches.shape: Line 1 names the fight. Line 2 is the choice. Line 3 is the consequence. Stop.
niches.tools: A still or video generator, your voice, CapCut.
niches.avoid: Five scenes in 15 seconds, or a different painter every episode.

niches.name: Character dance
niches.about: A character you made, placed on a dance you can use.
niches.lasts: The sound peaks in a few days. The character can outlast the sound.
steps: Use a dance clip you have the rights to. One person, full body, 8 to 15 seconds.
Make a character. Do not use a living person's photo, and do not use a celebrity.
Put the still onto the dance with a motion tool. Export vertical.
Keep the face sharp. If the hands melt, redo that take.
Same character next time, new sound only if you can use it.
Label the video as AI.
niches.shape: No dialogue. The first frame is the character already moving. A caption names them.
niches.tools: A motion tool such as Viggle or Kling, plus CapCut.
niches.avoid: A private person's face, or a celebrity's face, on the dance.

niches.name: Object characters
niches.about: A vegetable, a cat, or a tool with a face, doing one human action.
niches.lasts: The object is the series. A new object every day resets the channel.
steps: Pick one object and give it a face you can redraw.
One action only: dancing, cooking, or answering a phone.
Keep the object readable. If it turns into a person, you lost the joke.
Add one caption. Do not narrate a plot.
Label it AI.
Next video is the same object in a new room, or the same action with a second object.
niches.shape: Frame 1: the object is already in the action. Caption: what they think they are doing.
niches.tools: A still or video generator, CapCut.
niches.avoid: A real pet's owner footage passed off as yours, or a new mascot every upload.

niches.name: AI love story
niches.about: A short romance. The last scene changes what the first scene meant.
niches.lasts: A kiss clip is one post. A couple with names can be a serial.
steps: Name both people and save their faces. Original adults. Not a real couple.
Write five lines: meeting, a promise, a doubt, a proof, a turn.
Show the promise on screen as text, so the turn can break it.
Use the same clothes and the same street so it feels like one story.
Caption the dialogue. Music stays under the lines.
Label it AI. Episode 2 starts from the turn, not from a new couple.
niches.shape: They meet. He promises one thing. She finds the opposite. The last line is his, and it is not an apology.
niches.tools: Stills or a video generator, your voice or on-screen text, CapCut.
niches.avoid: A real person's face as either lead, or a new couple every video.

niches.name: Real or AI
niches.about: The viewer has to guess which clip was generated. The answer is the ending.
niches.lasts: The format stays. Each clip is used once.
steps: Pick two clips of the same kind of shot: a face, a street, or an animal.
One must be generated by you. The other must be footage you can use.
Ask the question in the first second, in text, before either clip plays.
Hold each clip long enough to see one flaw or one real detail.
Reveal the answer in the last two seconds. Do not talk over the reveal.
Label the generated clip as AI in the caption.
niches.shape: Text: which one is AI? Clip A. Clip B. Text: B. One frozen frame of the tell.
niches.tools: A generator, footage you can use, CapCut.
niches.avoid: Using someone else's viral clip as the 'real' half without the right to use it.

niches.name: Original character talks
niches.about: One original adult character, to camera, one opinion per video.
niches.lasts: The character is the channel. A new face every week does not stick.
steps: Design one adult character. Do not copy a creator's face.
Write one opinion in four lines. The first line is the claim, not a hello.
Record it in your own voice, or use on-screen text if you will not show a cloned voice.
Same background, same clothes, same framing every time.
Caption the claim in the first second.
Label it AI. The next video is a new opinion, same person.
niches.shape: Line 1: the claim. Line 2: the example. Line 3: the mistake people make. Line 4: the claim again, shorter.
niches.tools: A still generator, your voice, a talking-photo tool, CapCut.
niches.avoid: A real creator's face, a minor's likeness, or a different character every upload.

niches.name: Hindi story episode
niches.about: A continuing story. Each video is one episode, and it ends on a question.
niches.lasts: Episode 1 can be small. The series is the product if the cliffhanger is real.
steps: Write the season in ten episodes before you generate anything.
Lock the cast. Same mother, same house, same neighbour.
Episode 1 starts in the problem. No theme song, no intro card longer than a second.
End on a line that episode 2 has to answer. Put 'Episode 1' on screen.
Caption in the language you are speaking. Keep the voice clear of music.
Label it AI. Upload the next episode while the first is still being shared.
niches.shape: She comes home. One thing is missing. She asks who took it. Cut before the answer.
niches.tools: A still or video generator, your voice, CapCut.
niches.avoid: A full movie in one Short, or a new cast in episode 2.

niches.name: One-twist short
niches.about: A one-off story with a single turn. Not a series.
niches.lasts: Each film stands alone. The style of the turn is what people come back for.
steps: Write the last line first. Then write only the setup that line needs.
Three shots: the normal world, the choice, the turn.
Say the character's name in the first line so the title is not doing that work.
No second twist. If you have one, cut it.
Hold the last frame for a beat with the line on screen.
Label it AI.
niches.shape: Ayesha takes one bite. She thinks it fixed the day. The last line says what the bite actually was.
niches.tools: A video generator, your voice, CapCut.
niches.avoid: A moral spoken after the twist, or a cast the viewer meets in the last second.

niches.name: One religious scene
niches.about: One scene from a known religious story, told as a story, labeled AI.
niches.lasts: A single verse clip spikes. A scene with the same art style can continue.
steps: Pick one scene you can tell in four lines. Not a whole scripture.
Use an illustrated style, not a real preacher's face or voice.
Put the scene's name on screen in the first second.
Read it in your own voice. Do not clone a reciter.
Caption every line.
Label it AI, in the video and in the caption, so it is not mistaken for a recording of a person.
niches.shape: Title of the scene. What was asked. What was done. The line people repeat.
niches.tools: An illustrated generator, your voice, CapCut.
niches.avoid: A real scholar's face, a cloned recitation, or presenting the clip as filmed history.

niches.name: Wedding-day drama
niches.about: One argument on a wedding day. The relationship is already known.
niches.lasts: One wedding is one post. A family, across episodes, is a serial.
steps: Start in the middle of the argument. Skip the baraat and the invitations.
Two people only. A third person can appear in the last line, not before.
The fight is about one object or one guest. Not about the whole marriage.
Same outfits if this is episode 2 of a family.
End on a line the other person does not answer.
Label it AI.
niches.shape: She asks where he was. He answers a different hour. She repeats the question. He names someone else.
niches.tools: Stills or a video generator, on-screen dialogue, CapCut.
niches.avoid: A real couple's photos, or a five-minute family tree before the fight.
